title: Voice Comic app protocol (vc.*) on top of RTVI 2.3.0
description: The app-level messages between the browser and the Pipecat bot. Everything else (user-input, bot-output, speaking events, metrics) is standard RTVI and is NOT redefined here. Server messages travel as the `data` of an RTVI `server-message` (RTVIServerMessageFrame); client messages travel as an RTVI `client-message` whose type is our `type` and whose data is the remaining fields. SessionConfig travels once, base64url-encoded JSON in the `cfg` query parameter of WS /api/agent. Field names are camelCase on the wire. Checked by server/tests/test_protocol_schema.py (pydantic models in server/vc/protocol.py) and web/src/lib/protocol.test.ts (types in web/src/lib/protocol.ts). Bump `protocolVersion` on any breaking change.

PanelId.description: Server-owned panel id convention. Flux turns: `u-{epoch}-{turnIndex}`; Nova tap / duet chunks: `n-{epoch}-{seq}`; typed lines: the client-chosen `k-...` id echoed back.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the STT stream (per socket; resets on reconnect, hence `epoch`).

SessionConfig.description: Everything needed to BUILD the pipeline. Sent once as the `cfg` query parameter; an experience change is a new connection.

speakers.description: Two speakers: run the Nova tap branch with diarize=true beside Flux.

PipelineStage.description: One processor as the X-ray draws it. Replaces the old 'Settings JSON'. Never contains secrets.

active.description: ServiceSwitcher members: which one is live.

settings.description: Public, non-secret settings (thresholds, redact, diarize, voice).

field.description: SessionConfig field that changed, or flux.eotThreshold / flux.eagerEotThreshold.

frame.description: Pipecat frame the server queued, e.g. STTUpdateSettingsFrame, ManuallySwitchServiceFrame, LLMUpdateSettingsFrame, branch-rebuild.

live.description: true = applied in place (Flux Configure, prompt swap); false = the service reconnects (Flux model, TTS voice/expressivity) and loses acoustic state.

withdrawnCalls.description: Speculative (eager) inferences discarded by UserTurnResponseCancelFrame: paid for, never spoken.

UsageReport.description: Server-metered, running totals for one connection. Built by vc.pipeline.observers.usage from MetricsFrame (STTUsageMetricsData, TTSUsageMetricsData, LLMUsageMetricsData). Saved with the strip; replaces the client estimate.

connectedMsByTier.description: Connection time attributed to the active LLM's Voice Agent tier. Only feeds the 'Voice Agent API equivalent' comparison. Zero in a duet.

sttSecondsByKey.description: Audio seconds sent per listen catalog key (Flux primary and Nova tap separately).

PanelMood.description: Robot expression chosen by Claude. smug and laughing map to the cast's happy face until C2 adds art.

PanelSfx.description: Each has a 24 kHz one-shot in server/vc/assets/sfx/ played into the bot audio, and a glyph in the panel.

VcSession.description: First message after RTVI client-ready. `id` is the metering key the client sends with POST /api/strips.

VcConfig.description: Sent after every vc.update / vc.reset is applied: the effective config, what was done, and the refreshed pipeline view. Replaces the Voice Agent *Updated acks; there is no ack timeout.

VcTurn.description: Flux turn layer from turn_tap, built from frame.result (raw TurnInfo) on the primary Flux STT. Drives the live visitor bubble, pace, shout and ZOOM.

epoch.description: Bumped each time the Flux socket (re)connects, because turn_index restarts per socket.

VcEager.description: Ghost bubble (beat 2). predicted: on_eager_end_of_turn. withdrawn: on_turn_resumed, or a UserTurnResponseCancelFrame seen by the eager observer. released: the held reply was let through (UserStoppedSpeakingFrame after a prediction). Nothing from the held reply itself is ever sent before release.

heldMs.description: released only: ms between predicted and released (the latency eager bought).

VcLayer.description: Nova-3 tap (Redact / Two speakers) and the whole duet. Emitted by nova_tap, which consumes the Nova TranscriptionFrame/InterimTranscriptionFrame so they never reach the user aggregator. In a diarized final, each contiguous speaker run is its own message.

VcIntel.description: themes_intel: /v1/read topics + intents on a finished visitor turn, fire-and-forget, off the critical path. Mood comes from perception now; sentiment is optional and only for the X-ray.

VcPanel.description: Beat 3: Claude's inline <panel mood=... sfx=... caption=.../> tag, stripped from the spoken text by panel_tags. Fires at LLM-output time, ahead of the audio: the client applies it when the bot-output spoken progress of that assistant turn reaches `at`.

assistantTurn.description: Count of LLMFullResponseStartFrame seen downstream of the LLM on this connection; the client counts onBotLlmStarted the same way.

at.description: Character offset in the turn's spoken (tag-free) text where the tag appeared.

VcLatency.description: The 'replied in X.Xs' stamp. TurnLatencyObserver (custom): Flux end of turn (ProposedUserStoppedSpeakingFrame) to BotStartedSpeakingFrame. For a typed line: LLMMessagesAppendFrame to BotStartedSpeakingFrame.

eager.description: The reply was a released speculation.

VcLatencyBreakdown.description: Beat 5: UserBotLatencyObserver on_latency_breakdown (VAD stop to bot speech), forwarded verbatim-ish for the latency pill and X-ray.

VcUsage.description: Throttled to at most one per second while metrics flow, plus one on disconnect.

message.description: Human-readable, already scrubbed (no keys, no transcript text).

VcUpdate.description: Any subset of the mutable config. experience is NOT here: a scene change is a new connection. Server answers with vc.config (or vc.error).

VcSay.description: Operator typed line: LLMMessagesAppendFrame([user], run_llm=True). Not echoed back as user text; the client drew it already. Refused in a duet.

VcReset.description: New conversation without reconnecting: InterruptionFrame, LLMMessagesUpdateFrame(messages=[]), then the greeting unless quiet. In a duet it only bumps the panel epoch.
